newsitem.title: USA: A.M. Castle sees $4-$6 mln in cost savings.
newsitem.headline: A.M. Castle sees $4-$6 mln in cost savings.

text.p: A.M. Castle & Co, a specialty metals maker, said Wednesday it expects to see about $4 million to $6 million in cost savings by the second quarter of 1998 from cost reduction initiatives.
Those intitiatives include improving the self sufficiency of stocking locations, consolidating the transportation supply base and streamlining administrative support systems, the company said.

"During the second quarter, our operating environment mirrored what we saw in the first three months of the year - stable, historically healthy levels of demand for highly engineered metals coupled with essentially flat pricing," chief executive officer Richard Mork said in a news release.
Earlier Wednesday, the company reported second quarter net income of $6.1 million, or $0.44 a share, compared to $7.0 million, or $0.50 a share, a year ago.
A.M. Castle shares closed up 7/16 at 22-15/16 Wednesday.
